title: The Morning Brief: Mayfield locked in; SEC votes on LSU today; US Open semifinals set
dek: Baker Mayfield's contract standoff with Tampa Bay ended Tuesday with a $165 million extension that ties him for the third-highest-paid QB in football. Meanwhile, the SEC votes Thursday on expulsion of LSU over NFL player recruitment, the College Football Playoff opens formal talks on 24-team expansion, and American men reach the US Open semifinals for the first time since 2003.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Thursday brings the SEC's first expulsion vote in the conference's 94-year history, a deadline that will reveal whether the league can enforce its governance against a major program and set a precedent for conference authority in college sports.
bottom_line: Thursday brings the SEC's first expulsion vote in conference history, testing whether leagues can enforce rules when state courts and player leverage push back. Separately, Mayfield's contract settlement and the CFP's 30-day negotiating window with ESPN mark two players and a governance structure both finding their price after months of standoff. The US Open semifinals guarantee an American finalist for the first time in 23 years. Watch for the SEC's two-thirds vote Thursday, whether LSU's state court injunction survives conference discipline, the CFP-ESPN talks through December 1, and whether the Seahawks can field a healthy QB rotation for Week 2.
body: The defining thread across Thursday's landscape is the collision between institutional power and the athletes themselves. Mayfield's contract reflects a player who publicly fought his employer and won; the SEC vote today tests whether conferences can still enforce rules on schools when players and state courts push back; the CFP's 30-day window with ESPN explores how to reshape college football's structure while keeping money moving; and two Americans reaching the US Open semis for the first time in 23 years underscores the deep talent pool the professional tour now operates in.

Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers settled their months-long dispute on September 8 with a three-year, $165 million extension at $55 million average annual value, tying him with Joe Burrow, Josh Allen, Jordan Love, Trevor Lawrence, and Matthew Stafford for the third-highest-paid quarterback in the NFL, per the desk's reporting. Mayfield becomes the highest-paid player in franchise history. The contract moves into effect immediately as the 2026 season begins. The reporting notes that Mayfield had publicly criticized the Buccaneers for undervaluing him in June and July; the final terms stretched his prior offer from two years into three, a structural victory that reflects his leverage after the 2024 MVP-caliber season.

The SEC, meanwhile, triggered the most significant governance test in the conference's modern history. The league filed an amended federal complaint Tuesday and scheduled a vote for Thursday, September 10, seeking legal authority to expel LSU over the school's recruitment and rostering of players with NFL contracts. The vote will determine whether the SEC can assemble the required two-thirds majority from university presidents. In the SEC's 94-year history, no member school has ever voted to expel another; the only separations came when schools chose to leave. LSU did not roster tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive lineman Zxavian Harris for the season opener against Clemson, both of whom had previously signed with NFL teams. Harris signed with the Saints and received $190 for gas; Wright signed with the Browns after being released by the Eagles. Both players said they could earn six figures playing for LSU this fall, per the desk's reporting. A Louisiana state court has already issued a preliminary injunction clearing the players to compete, creating a direct conflict between state authority and conference jurisdiction that could reach federal court. The SEC's complaint mentions LSU head coach Lane Kiffin 32 times across 44 pages; Kiffin has denied the allegations. The desk's reporting indicates multiple sources believed the league had the necessary votes for expulsion if LSU refused to de-escalate.

In college football governance writ large, the College Football Playoff triggered a mandatory 30-day negotiating window with ESPN on September 8 over a potential 24-team playoff expansion beginning in 2027. The CFP's statement emphasized this does not represent a commitment, only an opportunity to gather information. The window gives ESPN and the CFP until December 1 to reach agreement on revised media rights. On that same date, conferences must notify their broadcast partners whether they intend to drop conference championship games, linking format decisions directly to scheduling and media revenue. ESPN's reporting indicates the loss of conference championship games would cost ESPN at least $200 million in annual media value. The Big Ten and SEC control the expansion outcome under the CFP's governance structure, per the desk's bottom-line reporting.

Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe both advanced to the US Open men's semifinals on September 9, guaranteeing an American finalist for the first time since Andy Roddick won the title in 2003. Shelton, seeded eighth, defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) in the latest finish in US Open history, ending at 3:34 a.m. ET. The match lasted 4 hours and 28 minutes. This marked Shelton's first win over a top-three player in 17 attempts, per ESPN. Tiafoe defeated Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6) in a five-set quarterfinal comeback lasting 4 hours and 38 minutes, the first two-set-down comeback in a US Open men's quarterfinal since Roger Federer defeated Gael Monfils in 2014. Shelton and Tiafoe will meet Friday in the semifinal. On the women's side, all four top seeds reached the semifinals, the first time that has occurred at the US Open since 1975. Aryna Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina, Jessica Pegula, and Coco Gauff will contest the final four, with Sabalenka facing Pegula on September 12.

In the NFL, the Seattle Seahawks defeated the New England Patriots 13-10 in the season opener on September 10, a rematch of last year's Super Bowl. Patriots QB Drake Maye threw an interception to Seahawks cornerback Josh Jobe in the end zone with 26 seconds remaining at the Seattle 16-yard line on third-and-5, ending the game. The Patriots had field-goal range and overtime available, per NBC's commentary. Seahawks QB Sam Darnold suffered a hip injury on the opening drive and was ruled out before halftime; a fracture was ruled out, but further testing was pending.

Other significant moves: the Dodgers called up prospect Josue De Paula, MLB Pipeline's No. 6 overall prospect, to make his major league debut Friday in Miami after placing Shohei Ohtani on the 15-day injured list with left knee and right biceps injuries. The Big Ten announced Wednesday it will broadcast live audio between referees and replay officials during all conference games and home non-conference matchups officiated by Big Ten officials beginning Saturday, September 12, following a controversial clock discrepancy in last weekend's Michigan-Western Michigan game. The College Sports Commission cleared $227 million in NIL deals during July and August 2026, nearly double the value of all deals processed in its first year, per ESPN's reporting. The Rugby Football Union will extend Steve Borthwick's contract past the 2028 Six Nations heading into the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia, though his future beyond the tournament depends entirely on World Cup performance. LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy Tuesday in New Jersey after the Saudi PIF ended funding, with a restructuring support agreement from BC Partners Credit and a January 2027 emergence target; the league estimates liabilities between $500 million and $1 billion.
